original_text: SETTLING BREAKUP SELECTION RULE (breakup.toml, authoritative over results/breakup-field-candidate.md): the inputs are vertical and total specific kinetic energy, written as speeds V_d and V; the flight-path angle is implied by the two. P(intact) = L(ln(a/V_d)/s)·L(ln(c/V)/s); P(fragmented) = (1−P(intact))·L(ln(V/b)/s); broken is the remainder. Constants: a = 8 m/s, c = 100 m/s, b = 110 m/s, s = 0.2. Calibration anchors, each checked against its primary report: US1549 (64 m/s, 3.81 m/s down per NTSB AAR-10/03) → P(intact) 0.882; AF447 (78, 55) → P(broken) 0.848; Swissair 111 (154 m/s, 20° nose down per TSB A98H0003) → P(fragmented) 0.843. Mass shares sum to 1 per family, and the rule refuses rather than guesses when mass or energy is missing.

original_text: The seabed-search detectable-target definition (results/seabed-detectable-target.md) fixes detection as a TWO-PART event: at least one wreckage piece in the detectable class (piece level), then recognition (CAMPAIGN level, never per piece — independent per-piece classification would collapse the likelihood to a hard exclusion wherever coverage exists). This gives M_k = 1 - c_k·g_k(W)·q_k with g_k = 1 - prod_i[1 - a_k(L_i)], which reduces exactly to Davey eq. 11.1 for a point target. A field partly inside a swath is scored coarse-grained (in or out as a whole), with the fine-grained arm as a labelled sensitivity, because coverage gaps are at the same scale as the field.

original_text: g_k saturates: a field of even a few dozen pieces with some metres across on flat abyssal seabed gives g_k indistinguishable from 1, so the likelihood collapses to the point-target form. Effort spent refining the piece-size distribution will not move the posterior; the uncertainty budget belongs to rho and the coverage rasters.

original_text: WHY THE SEABED-SEARCH RESIDUAL IS WIDER, NOT NARROWER (recorded in results/seabed-search-why-wider.md). The non-detection likelihood is bounded, not a veto: P(no find) = 1.000 off searched ground against 0.102 on fully covered Phase 2 ground at rho=0.05, q=0.945, a factor of 9.8. The posterior is renormalised by Z, so unsearched ground is multiplied by 1/Z (1.45 held out, 1.97 for R600 BTO + Raw BFO) and becomes ABSOLUTELY denser; flank cells just below the 90% threshold cross it, while the searched corridor - which runs through the MIDDLE of the distribution along the 7th arc, not around its rim - is pushed down five- to sevenfold. The 50% region holds or shrinks (+1%, -18%, +4% in the estimable core options); only the 90% and 99% shoulders spread. Within this model a BETTER search (higher q, lower rho) widens the residual further, because it deepens the trough; the region only shrinks once coverage leaves a remainder that is small in its own right.
